 Has the stock market’s slump hit bottom yet? Here’s what these contrarian indicators say.
 Mark Hulbert Wed, November 18, 2026 at 1:58 PM PST 3 min read We're not at the bottom yet, it appears. - Getty Images/iStockphoto The bottom of the stock market's slump is still ahead of us, according to contrarian analysis. 
 That surprises some traders, since the stock market's recent declines and extraordinary volatility has caused the mood on Wall Street to sour. Surely the veritable Wall of Worry that markets like to climb has been sufficiently rebuilt?

 No, according to my auditing firm's monitoring of short-term market timers. Though it is true that they are less bullish than they were six weeks ago, they have not yet become bearish enough to satisfy contrarians' criteria for a buy signal. 
 Consider these timers' average recommended equity exposure level. The Hulbert Stock Newsletter Sentiment Index (HSNSI), which reflects this average among several dozen short-term market timers who focus on the broad stock market. As you can see from the accompanying chart, it has declined to just the upper edge of the excessively bearish zone that I have used in prior columns about market sentiment. That zone is defined as the range of readings in the bottom decile of the historical distribution. 
 - Contrarian buy signals typically don't come until sentiment has dropped further into that zone and stays there for a number of trading sessions. 
 An even stronger indication that a buy signal would be premature comes from the Hulbert Nasdaq Newsletter Sentiment Index (HNNSI), which is a similar sentiment measure except that it includes a different group of timers — those who focus on the Nasdaq market in particular. (This second index is not in the accompanying chart.) This index has dropped even less than the HSNSI, which is surprising since the Nasdaq market has suffered significantly more in recent weeks than the broad market. While the S&P 500 SPX is 6.3% below its early October high, for example, the Nasdaq Composite COMP is 11.5% below. 
 Other sentiment measures are also suggesting that the decline has further to go. Consider the weekly sentiment survey that the American Association of Individual Investors conducts of its members. Those who say they are bullish, expressed as a percentage of those who are either bullish or bearish, just this week dipped to the upper end of what I have defined as the excessively bearish zone. The VIX VIX (Cboe's Volatility Index, aka the investor-fear index) is currently pointing away from being in its excessively bearish zone. 
 Story Continues Surging demand for Anthropic's upcoming IPO provides yet more evidence of these pockets of bullishness. The company's IPO reportedly has been nearly seven times oversubscribed . 
 The bottom line: Sentiment is moving in the right direction to entice contrarians to declare that a tradable bottom is in. But it's not there yet.
